Residents work in manufacturing, commerce, services and government, with some in mining and a few hundred on farms. The encyclopedia lists bituminous coal, limestone quarries, timber, fruit farms, tobacco and livestock among the county's resources.

Tourism has grown around Summersville Lake, which President Lyndon Johnson dedicated on September 3, 1966. It is the largest impoundment in the state, with about 2,800 acres of surface and 60 miles of shoreline, and it joined the state park system in 2023. Each fall the reservoir is lowered, which turns the lower Gauley into whitewater and brings a rafting season.

  • Carnifex Ferry Battlefield State Park marks an 1861 Civil War engagement.
  • Richwood hosts a ramp festival and Summersville a potato festival.
  • Vacation rentals, campgrounds and boat rentals serve lake and river visitors.
  • The county school system runs 15 schools with nearly 3,500 students, and public school enrollment was 3,382 in 2024-25.

The 2025 population estimate of 23,848 is 3.1 percent below the 2020 count. Median household income in the encyclopedia's fact box is $42,946, against $50,884 for the state.

The statewide calendar applies. Tickets come out on or after July 15, the first half is due September 1, and the second half is due March 1.

  • First-half tax that is still unpaid becomes delinquent on October 1.
  • Second-half tax becomes delinquent on April 1.

Parcels still delinquent on September 1 go on a second list that the sheriff prepares by September 10, and unredeemed liens are certified to the State Auditor on October 31 under West Virginia Code 11A-3-2. The owner can redeem before that date by paying the tax, interest and charges, which include $25 for the list and $10 for each mailed notice.

You raise it with the assessor and then with the county commission acting as the board of equalization and review. We could not find a Nicholas County notice with this year's dates on an opened county page, so the dates below are the ones in the statute.

West Virginia Code 11-3-24 requires the commission to meet as the board no later than February 1. It may adjourn after February 15 and must finish by the end of February. The board corrects errors and brings anything assessed at more or less than 60 percent of market value to 60 percent, and no increase can come without five days of written notice. Skipping the meeting waives the correction for that year except through an appeal to the Office of Tax Appeals. Questions about class or taxability are outside the board's reach and follow a protest route to the assessor.

Who qualifies for the Nicholas County homestead exemption?

Owners aged 65 or older, and owners certified as permanently and totally disabled, can exempt the first $20,000 of assessed value of an owner-occupied home. West Virginia Code 11-6B-3 also requires two consecutive calendar years of state residency, with exceptions for returning residents and military retirees.

The exemption belongs to the owner on the July 1 assessment date. When the house changes hands by deed or will, it comes off on the next July 1 unless the new owner qualifies. Under that wording, a house sold in March keeps the old owner's exemption until the following July.

What should you know about selling a Nicholas County house with tax due?

The buyer's title company will look for unpaid tickets, so deal with them first. Start with the Sheriff's Tax Office and ask for the balance on each tax year, including fire fee charges, which the office's online system lists.

The deed has to be recorded with the county clerk, and the transfer tax is set by West Virginia Code 11-22-2: $1.10 per $500 of value, kept by the county since July 1, 2025, plus an additional county tax of 55 cents per $500 unless the commission raised it, plus a $20 fee. On a $90,000 sale at those base rates that is $198, $99 and $20, so $317. The seller pays unless the buyer accepts the deed with the tax unpaid.

Flooding is part of the local record: the encyclopedia says a deadly 2016 flood along the Cherry River devastated Richwood and other places in the county, so ask any buyer or insurer about flood history for a Richwood address.

Do I owe property tax if I sell my Nicholas County house mid-year?

The tax for the year is a lien on the property, so any unpaid ticket must be settled at or before closing. Ask the sheriff's office for the balance and have the title company confirm it.

How is a Nicholas County home assessed?

The assessor values it at 60 percent of market value, and the owner's class sets the rate. Owner-occupied residential property is Class II, which the state publication says is taxed at twice the Class I rate, while other real estate outside or inside municipalities is taxed at four times Class I.

The Mason-Dixon Line forms the northern boundary, and part of the Monongahela National Forest, Cathedral State Park and Fairfax Stone State Park lie within it.

Besides Kingwood the county has nine towns: Albright, Brandonville, Bruceton Mills, Masontown, Newburg, Reedsville, Rowlesburg, Terra Alta and Tunnelton. Arthurdale and Aurora are census-designated places. Eight old magisterial districts were merged into five numbered districts in the 1990s.

What does winter mean for a Preston County house?

Terra Alta in Preston County holds the state's record monthly snowfall, 104 inches in January 1977. The encyclopedia adds that cold weather sometimes strays into other seasons, and that a frost on June 5, 1859, killed crops in the fields.

That matters to anyone selling an old farm or a parcel with a long chain of title. Deeds from before 1869 may be missing from the courthouse, so a title search can lean on later deeds, surveys and the assessor's tax maps. If a parcel has been in a family for generations, start the paperwork early.

The B&O Railroad arrived in the 1850s and opened markets for timber and coal. Newburg grew as a coal and railroad town, and an explosion at the Orrel Coal Company shaft in January 1886 killed 39 men. The county's population was 3,422 in 1820 and reached a high in the 2020 census.

Agriculture, coal and timber remain part of the economy, joined by education, health care, technology, tourism and historic preservation. The encyclopedia also notes the satellite earth station at Etam, which links into an international communications system.

Preston County is part of the Morgantown metropolitan area, and Interstate 68 across the north of the county eases the drive between Monongalia County and Maryland. Other roads include U.S. 50 in the south, U.S. 219, and West Virginia routes 7, 24, 26, 72 and 92. Preston High School at Kingwood serves the whole county, and public school enrollment was 3,872 in 2024-25.

A $125,000 deed at those base rates is $275, $137.50 and $20, or $432.50. The grantor pays unless the grantee accepts the deed without the tax being paid.

When are Preston County property taxes due?

The first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1. Paying before either date earns a 2.5 percent discount, and unpaid halves become delinquent on October 1 and April 1.

Where do I pay property tax in Preston County?

Pay at the Sheriff's Tax Office at 106 West Main Street in Kingwood, phone 304-329-0105, or online through the county's vendor link. Sources list the suite as 101 or 102, so call ahead.

Is there an assessment appeal deadline in Preston County?

The statute has the county commission meet as the board of equalization and review by February 1 and finish by the end of February. We did not find a Preston County notice with this year's exact dates, so confirm with the assessor at 304-329-1220.

What happens if my Preston County taxes go unpaid?

They accrue 9 percent interest from the delinquency date. A parcel still delinquent on September 1 goes on the sheriff's second list, and the lien can be certified to the State Auditor on October 31.

Do old Preston County deeds exist from before 1869?

Many may not. The encyclopedia says an arson fire in 1869 destroyed most county records from 1818 to 1869, so a title search on an old parcel can depend on later deeds and surveys.

Where is Barbour County, West Virginia, and what is it like?

Barbour County sits on the Allegheny Plateau in north-central West Virginia, with Philippi as the county seat. It covers 342.9 square miles of mountainous country drained by the Buckhannon, Middle Fork and Tygart Valley rivers.

The Virginia legislature created the county on March 3, 1843, from parts of Lewis, Harrison and Randolph counties, and named it for the Virginia jurist Philip Pendleton Barbour. It borders Taylor and Preston counties to the north, Tucker and Randolph to the east, Upshur to the south and Harrison to the west. Laurel Mountain, the westernmost of the high Allegheny ridges, marks the eastern edge.

U.S. 119 and U.S. 250 run the length of the county, north to south, and U.S. 33 cuts across the southern tip. Philippi had 2,928 residents in 2020 and Belington, the second-largest town, had 1,804.

What are the key Barbour County numbers for an owner or seller?

What is the history of Barbour County and Philippi?

Philippi was the site of what is generally considered the first land battle of the Civil War among organized troops, fought before dawn on June 3, 1861. About 3,000 federal troops under Col. Benjamin F. Kelley routed roughly 800 newly recruited Confederates. The Battle of Belington, or Laurel Mountain, followed on July 7 to 11, 1861.

Philippi's covered bridge, which carries U.S. 250 across the Tygart Valley River, was built by Lemuel Chenoweth in 1852 and is still the town's best-known landmark. The railroad reached Philippi on January 25, 1884. The last passenger train stopped there in 1956, and the line now carries only freight. The 1911 depot has been the Barbour County Historical Museum since 1979.

The county courthouse was completed in 1905. If you hold an older house in the county, a deed or survey may reference these historic roads and river bottoms, so keep the paperwork together for a buyer.

How does flooding affect houses in Philippi and Barbour County?

Philippi sits mostly on low bottomland along the Tygart Valley River, and it has flooded repeatedly. The most damaging flood came in November 1985, and the town has since adopted a floodplain management plan.

If you own a house in a river bottom, take these steps before you sell:

  • Ask your insurer or title company whether the parcel is in a mapped flood zone.
  • Collect any repair invoices from past water damage.
  • Disclose past water in the basement or crawl space to every buyer.
  • Find out whether the lender on a financed buyer will require flood insurance.

Flood questions slow down financed purchases, since lenders and insurers have to sign off. A buyer paying cash does not need a lender's approval, though a careful buyer will still look at the risk.

What drives the Barbour County economy?

Natural resources have defined the local economy: coal, gas and timber, plus family farms in the valleys. Hardwood logging boomed at the start of the twentieth century, and second- and third-growth timber is still cut each year. Oil reserves were mostly depleted early in the century.

Coal output fell from a 1948 high of 3,895,803 tons to just over 2.3 million tons in 2021, then rose to more than five million tons by 2025, making Barbour the state's ninth-leading coal county and one of the fastest-growing. That swing shows how closely household finances here can follow commodity cycles.

Alderson Broaddus University, a Baptist institution that began as Broaddus Institute in 1909 in Philippi, closed permanently in 2023. Owners near the former campus who counted on university-related demand should ask a local agent or appraiser how the closure has affected their street.

How is West Virginia property tax assessed, and how does Barbour County fit in?

West Virginia assesses all real and tangible personal property, with limited exceptions. As of July 1 each year the ownership, use and value of property are fixed for the next calendar tax year. The county assessor values your property, and the county sheriff bills and collects the tax.

The state constitution divides property into four classes:

  • Class I: intangible personal property and certain farm personal property. Nothing is currently taxed in this class.
  • Class II: owner-occupied residential property used only for residence, and farmland used for agriculture by its owner or a bona fide tenant.
  • Class III: property outside a municipality that is not in Class I or II.
  • Class IV: property inside a municipality that is not in Class I or II.

That matters at a sale. A house you live in is Class II, while a rental or vacant house falls in Class III or IV depending on where it sits, so the tax can change after the buyer takes ownership. Property tax is levied by county boards of education, county commissions, municipalities and the State.

Protests of an assessment must be filed with the county commission sitting as a board of equalization and review, which begins meeting on February 1 and must adjourn by February 28. The protest has to come before the taxes are due for that year. A disagreement over classification or taxability can go to the Tax Commissioner under West Virginia Code 11-3-24a, and the ruling is due by the end of February.

Who qualifies for the West Virginia homestead exemption?

West Virginia Code 11-6B-3 exempts the first $20,000 of assessed value of a homestead from ad valorem tax. The owner must be 65 or older, or certified as permanently and totally disabled, and must use and occupy the home only as a residence.

The owner must also have been a West Virginia resident for the two consecutive calendar years before the tax year. An owner who receives a similar exemption in another state is not eligible.

If you plan to sell, the exemption matters less to you than to the buyer. A new owner under 65 will not carry it over, so the tax bill may rise. Mention that to a financed buyer's agent so there is no surprise at the first tax ticket.

How does a cash sale work in Barbour County?

A cash sale in Barbour County follows the normal West Virginia closing steps without a buyer's mortgage. You describe the house, receive a written offer and choose whether to accept. An attorney or title company records the deed, pays off liens and settles any tax due.

Cash Home Buyers buys houses as-is. We charge no fees, commissions or closing costs, and you owe nothing if you decline. If taxes are unpaid, ask the sheriff's tax office for the balance before you set a closing date, because unpaid current-year tax can be settled out of your proceeds.

  • Long distances for buyers, which can mean fewer showings on a listed house.
  • Older houses with plumbing, roof or septic questions.
  • Inherited property with several heirs in different states.

When are Barbour County property taxes due?

Tax tickets are issued on or after July 15. The first installment is due September 1 and the second March 1, with delinquency starting October 1 and April 1.

How do I protest my Barbour County assessment?

File a protest with the county commission sitting as the board of equalization and review. It begins meeting on February 1 and must adjourn by February 28, before the taxes are due.

Who gets the West Virginia homestead exemption?

Owners 65 or older, or permanently and totally disabled, who live in the home can exempt the first $20,000 of assessed value. The application deadline is December 1.

Is Philippi in a flood area?

Much of Philippi is low bottomland along the Tygart Valley River and has flooded, most severely in November 1985. Ask your insurer or title company about your parcel.

Can I sell a Barbour County house with unpaid taxes?

Yes. The unpaid tax is usually paid from the sale proceeds at closing. Get a balance from the sheriff's tax office first.

Harrison County by the numbers

What is Harrison County, West Virginia, and who taxes property there?

Harrison County is in north-central West Virginia, with Clarksburg as its seat. It was organized on May 3, 1784, from part of Monongalia County and named for Benjamin Harrison V, and it covers 417 square miles. Over the following 72 years, eight present-day West Virginia counties and pieces of ten others were carved out of the original Harrison County.

Bridgeport, Clarksburg, Salem, Shinnston, Stonewood, Anmoore, Lumberport, Nutter Fort and West Milford are among its incorporated places. Interstate 79 runs through the county with U.S. 19 and U.S. 50, and the West Fork River and Tenmile Creek are the main waterways. Four taxing bodies bill against a Harrison County parcel: the state, the county commission, the county board of education and, inside a municipality, the city or town.

What drives the Harrison County economy and housing demand?

Harrison County grew as a rail and coal county and now leans on health care, federal employment and offices along I-79. The Northwestern Turnpike reached Clarksburg in 1836, and the Baltimore and Ohio Railroad arrived in 1856, which helped build the local coal mining industry. Glass and other manufacturing followed.

Today the county's larger employers include United Hospital Center and the FBI's Criminal Justice Information Services Division. The FBI says most of the division's roughly 3,500 employees and contractors work in two main buildings. Technology and business sites also line the Interstate 79 corridor, which is sometimes called the I-79 High Tech Corridor.

A large employer does not fix an individual house with a failing roof or a tenant problem. Sellers with those issues still price against what a buyer will pay after repairs.

Who do you call about Harrison County property tax?

The assessor values property and the sheriff collects the tax, and both are in the General Services Building at 229 South Third Street in Clarksburg. The Assessor's Office is at 304-624-8510 and the Sheriff's taxes-due line is 304-624-8685. The assessor's site lists separate numbers for individual assessments, business assessments, mobile homes, homestead exemptions and oil and gas.

  • Taxes due (how much you owe): 304-624-8685.
  • Homestead exemptions: 304-624-8540.
  • Mobile home assessments: 304-624-8517.
  • Oil and gas and minerals division: 304-624-8523.

The office also posts summer satellite days at places such as Meadowbrook Mall, the Clarksburg Senior Center and several fire stations, so people in Shinnston, Lost Creek or Spelter do not always need to drive downtown. Filing is also available online through the state's SmartFile system.

What filing dates matter to Harrison County owners?

The assessor's 2026 filing season runs from July 1, and the key dates differ by form. Individual personal property returns are due between July 1 and October 1, and business personal property returns and farm exemption applications between July 1 and September 1. Homestead exemption applications can be filed from July 1 through December 1 to take effect for the following tax year.

Tax tickets themselves follow the state schedule. They are issued on or after July 15, the first installment is due September 1, the second March 1, and a 2.5 percent discount applies before those dates. Unpaid first-half tax becomes delinquent on October 1 and second-half tax on April 1, with 9 percent annual interest.

West Virginia's homestead exemption removes the first $20,000 of assessed value for an owner who is 65 or older or certified permanently and totally disabled, and who meets the residency rule. A seller who qualifies should confirm the exemption was actually filed, since a missed filing means a higher bill on a house about to be sold.

How do Harrison County owners appeal a valuation?

Talk to the Assessor's Office first, then take the dispute to the Harrison County Commission sitting as the Board of Equalization and Review, which meets from February 1 and finishes by February 28. The board can reduce a value that exceeds 60 percent of true and actual value, and it must give written notice at least five days before raising one.

If the board rules against you, the next step is the Office of Tax Appeals, with a petition due by March 31 of the tax year. Missing the February window waives the right to argue that year's list. Dispute over whether a home is Class II or Class IV is handled separately with the assessor and the Tax Commissioner.

Evidence that works is concrete: a recent appraisal, a repair estimate for a damaged structure, or sales of similar homes. For a house you plan to sell soon, an appeal is often not worth the effort unless the value is clearly wrong, because the new owner will be assessed on the next cycle anyway.

What happens to unpaid tax and how does a cash sale handle it in Harrison County?

The sheriff certifies unpaid real estate tax for sale, and the State Auditor, not the sheriff, now runs the lien sale. An older tax lien sale FAQ posted on the county site says the sale was held between October 17 and November 24. Marion County's sheriff, a neighbor, explains the change in the law from the Legislature and a certification deadline of October 31.

Because rules shifted, call the Sheriff at 304-624-8685 before you assume anything about timing or redemption cost. A seller who owes tax can often clear it through closing: the title company obtains a payoff and pays it from the proceeds. The county excise tax on a recorded deed is 55 cents for each $500 of value under the transfer tax statute.

We buy houses in Harrison County as-is, so a house in Clarksburg that needs a roof, has a tenant, or carries back taxes does not need to be fixed first. Call or text (424) 435-2326 for a written cash offer.

Do minerals and mobile homes change a Harrison County tax picture?

They can, because the Assessor's Office keeps separate divisions for mobile homes and for oil, gas and minerals. A mobile home may be assessed through its own desk at 304-624-8517, and oil and gas or mineral matters go to 304-624-8523. The state also runs its own appraisal process for oil and gas royalties.

When you sell, ask the assessor and your title company whether any mineral interest is tied to the parcel and whether it carries its own assessment. Deeds do not always say, and a buyer will want a clear answer. Cash buyers are generally fine with houses where title questions like this need work, and we check before we make an offer.

West Virginia's four classes also matter. Class II covers owner-occupied residential property used exclusively as a home. Property in a municipality that does not qualify, such as a rental house in Clarksburg, falls in Class IV, and property outside a municipality falls in Class III. Those classes have higher regular ceilings than Class II.

More questions about Harrison County, WV Property Tax Guide

When are Harrison County property taxes due?

Half is due September 1 and half March 1, and a 2.5 percent discount applies if you pay before each date. Taxes unpaid after October 1 (first half) or April 1 (second half) are delinquent and accrue 9 percent yearly interest.

Where is the Harrison County Sheriff's tax office?

It is at 229 South 3rd Street, Clarksburg, WV 26301, and the phone for taxes due is 304-624-8685. Online payment is also offered.

When can I apply for the homestead exemption in Harrison County?

Eligible homeowners apply between July 1 and December 1 to receive the exemption for the following tax year. It covers the first $20,000 of assessed value for owners 65 or older or permanently and totally disabled.

What is the deadline to appeal a Harrison County assessment?

Protest to the county commission sitting as the Board of Equalization and Review, which starts February 1 and ends by February 28. An appeal to the Office of Tax Appeals is due March 31.

Can I sell a Harrison County house that has back taxes?

Yes. A title company can get a payoff for the unpaid tax and pay it from the sale proceeds at closing.
